title: JetBrains 2026.1 IDE MCP — Database Access and IDE Actions for Agents
description: JetBrains released IntelliJ IDEA 2026.1 and PhpStorm 2026.1 in March 2026, adding significant new MCP capabilities: (1) database access for AI agents — Claude Agent and Codex can now query and modify IDE-connected data sources natively, (2) access to IDE actions — agents can trigger arbitrary IDE actions (setup, customization, refactoring), (3) structural search — agents can use IntelliJ's semantic code pattern matching, (4) a companion Claude Code plugin providing Claude Code context and instructions for using PhpStorm MCP tools. The ACP Agent Registry (launched Jan 2026 with JetBrains + Zed) provides discovery of compatible agents.
redundancy_notes: No JetBrains/IntelliJ entry in registry. However, workspace uses VS Code (confirmed in CLAUDE.md development environment) — platform dependency makes this low-priority. Monitor for VS Code equivalent.

evaluation.reasoning: Score of 56 sits in NEEDS_RESEARCH band, but the primary blocker is a platform incompatibility, not missing information. Current dev environment is VS Code on native Linux (requiem) — integrating JetBrains MCP would require switching IDEs, making integration_complexity effectively very high (score: 20). The capabilities themselves are genuinely valuable: IDE-native structural search, DB access from agents, and arbitrary IDE action triggering would all expand capability (score: 65). Community validation is strong — JetBrains is a major IDE vendor, official 2026.1 release (score: 85). This item is NEEDS_RESEARCH rather than REJECTED because: (1) the ACP Agent Registry mentioned in this discovery is independently valuable and worth tracking, (2) a VS Code equivalent from JetBrains or Microsoft may be imminent. If VS Code equivalent launches, re-evaluate immediately.
evaluation.action: MONITOR: (1) Watch for VS Code equivalent of JetBrains MCP capabilities (structural search, IDE actions from agents). (2) Track ACP Agent Registry (JetBrains + Zed, launched Jan 2026) as a separate discovery candidate. (3) Re-evaluate if workspace switches to JetBrains or if VS Code ships equivalent tooling.
